comments.undefined:
The Atrial Fibrillation Monitoring Ontology (AFMO) extends the Personal Health Monitoring Ontology (PHMO) with concepts specific to atrial fibrillation (AF) monitoring.

From version 3.0, general personal health monitoring concepts have moved to the PHMO (http://purl.org/phmo), which the AFMO imports. Terms listed as deleted in the changelog have moved to the PHMO namespace.

In addition to the ontologies reused through the PHMO, the AFMO contains concepts reused from the following ontologies:

- Human Disease Ontology (DO)
- Medical Action Ontology (MAxO)

Health domain concepts have been manually cross-referenced to concepts from the Unified Medical Language System (UMLS) metathesaurus, which maps to several medical vocabularies and terminologies, including:

- SNOMED CT (US)
- Medical Subject Headings (MeSH) Thesaurus
- National Cancer Institute (NCI) Thesaurus
- MedlinePlus

isDefinedBy.value:
https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/nhis/tobacco/tobacco_recodes.htm#anchor_1557516509294 and the New Zealand Ministry of Health https://www.health.govt.nz/our-work/preventative-health-wellness/tobacco-control/tobacco-control-information-practitioners/definitions-smoking-status.

- Smoker (a.k.a current smoker): a person who has smoked more than 100 cigarettes (including hand rolled cigarettes, cigars, cigarillos etc) in their lifetime and has smoked in the last 28 days. Includes daily and non-daily/social smokers.
- Non-smoker: composed of two groups: former smoker and never smoker.
   - Former smoker: a person who has smoked more than 100 cigarettes in their lifetime but has not smoked in the last 28 days. The international convention is to treat someone as an ex-smoker once they have been smokefree for one month (at least 28 days).
   - Never smoker: a person who has not smoked more than 100 cigarettes in their lifetime and does not currently smoke.

Dagfinn et al. (2018) noted that there is reduced risk of AF among former smokers compared to current smokers, but further research is needed to determine if the risk at some point reaches that of never smokers.

The seca Scale-up Line is probably the most modern and pioneering option for determining size and weight. Firstly on account of the contactless, fast, and high-precision ultrasonic measurement. Secondly because of the ID-Display, which shows the names or IDs of patients and users during data transfer to the digital patient record (EMR). definition.value: Ethnicity is a term for the ethnic group to which people belong. Usually it refers to group identity based on culture, religion, traditions, and customs. In some contexts, it is a “politically correct” term equivalent to the word “race,” which may have pejorative associations.

Race is a social construct used to group people. Race was constructed as a hierarchal human-grouping system, generating racial classifications to identify, distinguish and marginalize some groups across nations, regions and the world. Race divides human populations into groups often based on physical appearance, social factors and cultural backgrounds.

definition.value: An obstructive lung disease that is a chronic and progressive disorder of small airways in the lungs and that is characterized by irreversible airflow obstruction, typically identified by reductions in quantitative spirometric indices, induced forced expiratory volume at 1 second (FEV1) and the ratio of FEV1 to forced vital capacity (less than 0.7 is diagnostic of COPD). Lung volume is increased and pulmonary hypertension may occur. The pathologic changes result in the disruption of the airflow in the bronchial airways. Signs and symptoms include shortness of breath, wheezing, productive cough and chest tightness. COPD is a consequence (an end result) of chronic bronchitis, emphysema or both.
